standard_prerequisites: Chapter Definition definition-set-theoretically-invariant (navigation stub): set-theoretically R-invariant means U(k) to X(k) equalizes s and t for every algebraically closed k over B; equivalently the equalizer Z below maps surjectively onto R on topological spaces, since every geometric point of R lifts to a k-point
X locally separated over B: the diagonal of X over B is an immersion, so the equalizer Z of the two maps from R to X times over B X, taken over the diagonal, is an immersion into R
Schemes, Lemma schemes-lemma-immersion-when-closed: an immersion whose image is closed is a closed immersion; in particular a bijective immersion is a closed immersion
A bijective closed immersion into a reduced algebraic space or scheme is an isomorphism: its defining quasi-coherent ideal sheaf consists of nilpotent sections and hence vanishes on a reduced target
core_obligations: Form the equalizer Z of the two maps from R to X times over B X obtained by composing j with phi, taken over the diagonal of X over B

Since X is locally separated over B the diagonal is an immersion, so the projection Z to R is an immersion; by set-theoretic R-invariance every geometric point of R lifts to Z, so the map on topological spaces from Z to R is surjective
A surjective immersion is a bijective immersion, hence a closed immersion by the schemes lemma; since R is reduced, a bijective closed immersion into R is an isomorphism, so Z equals R
Z equal to R means the two composites R to X times over B X agree, which is exactly phi composed with s equals phi composed with t; hence phi is R-invariant
proof_roadmap: Set up the equalizer of the two invariance composites and identify it as an immersion via local separatedness of the target
Upgrade set-theoretic invariance to surjectivity of the equalizer on points
Conclude with bijective immersion plus reducedness giving the identity of Z and R
